RUSTSEC-2021-0127 reports that serde_cbor is unmaintained with no active development or security fixes. The qdrant binary uses serde_cbor for CBOR serialization of internal data structures. While no specific vulnerability is identified, the lack of maintenance poses a long-term risk. Investigation is ongoing to assess migration to maintained alternatives such as ciborium or minicbor, but this requires upstream qdrant changes to maintain compatibility with existing data formats.

RUSTSEC-2025-0134 reports that rustls-pemfile is unmaintained with no active development or security fixes. The qdrant binary uses rustls-pemfile for parsing PEM-encoded TLS certificates and keys. While no specific vulnerability is identified, the lack of maintenance poses a long-term risk for TLS security. Investigation is ongoing to assess migration to maintained alternatives such as pem or x509-parser, but this requires upstream qdrant changes to maintain compatibility with existing TLS configuration.

RUSTSEC-2024-0436 reports that paste is unmaintained with no active development or security fixes. The qdrant binary uses paste as a procedural macro for code generation at compile time. While no specific vulnerability is identified and the macro only affects build-time code generation (not runtime behavior), the lack of maintenance poses a long-term risk. Investigation is ongoing to assess whether upstream qdrant can migrate to maintained alternatives or inline the macro functionality.

The Marvin timing side-channel (RUSTSEC-2023-0071) affects RSA private-key operations (PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption/signing). The qdrant binary in this image is installed from the dhi/pkg-qdrant package (built with `cargo auditable build --release --locked --bin qdrant --features stacktrace`). rsa 0.9.10 is compiled in only transitively, via jsonwebtoken (rust_crypto feature) - jsonwebtoken is rsa's sole reverse-dependency in the lockfile. qdrant's JWT RBAC is locked to HS256 (HMAC-SHA256): src/common/auth/jwt_parser.rs:15 sets `const ALGORITHM = Algorithm::HS256` and validation is pinned to it, using the API key as a symmetric secret. Production code only verifies tokens (`decode()`); the sole `encode()` call is test-only (`#[cfg(test)]`) and also HMAC. qdrant never performs an RSA private-key operation, so the vulnerable code path is not in the shipped binary's execute path.

The advisory is an unsoundness triggered only when a custom global logger calls rand::rng() reentrantly during thread-RNG initialization. The qdrant binary in this image is installed from the dhi/pkg-qdrant package (built with `cargo auditable build --release --locked --bin qdrant --features stacktrace`). qdrant installs no such logger (no set_logger / set_boxed_logger implementation that invokes rand), so the reentrant condition never occurs; rand is used only for ordinary shuffling/sampling.

CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

Backported the upstream IO::Compress IO::Uncompress::Unzip _dosToUnixTime hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched _dosToUnixTime short-circuits to 0 for a zero DOS datetime and wraps Time::Local::timelocal() in an eval guard so out-of-range month/day/hour values no longer raise an uncaught exception out of IO::Uncompress::Unzip->new($file), so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream IO::Compress zipdetails hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched zipdetails CLI calls the correctly spelled unpackValue_Q helper when decoding 8-byte UID/GID values from Info-ZIP Unix Extra Fields (closing the published undefined-subroutine crash), and decode_ux now validates the UID/GID Size byte through canDecodeLittleEndian and reports invalid or zero sizes as bad data instead of triggering internalFatal, so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.
